cases.reason: X is tighter, numbered for cover-and-recall and comes with a ready-made blanked self-quiz version and answer key, whereas Y is accurate but runs to several pages of essay-like content.

X builds spaced retrieval into every starter and has three checkpoints before the final assessment, though some lessons are overloaded; Y is more detailed per lesson but only retrieves the previous lesson and has no real checkpoint until the final week.

X follows a clear predict-modify-make progression with full test tables, staged hints and correct worked solutions, while Y jumps quickly to writing from scratch with fewer test cases and little support.
Both are strong, but Y's timings add up consistently and it produces a single named student sheet to collect, while X's timing table contradicts its own lesson outline.
